title: Divisibility, Factors, and Prime Numbers
subtitle: Discover factor pairs, proper divisors, and the prime building blocks of all integers.
challenge: Why can 12 objects be arranged into rectangles in several different ways (1×12, 2×6, 3×4), while 13 objects can only be formed into a single line (1×13)?

predictionOptions.label: Yes, because it is only divisible by 1 and itself
No, by definition a prime number must have exactly two distinct positive divisors

formalDefinition: An integer d divides an integer n (written d | n) if there exists an integer k such that n = d × k. A positive integer p > 1 is prime if its only positive divisors are 1 and p. An integer n > 1 that is not prime is composite. Every integer n > 1 can be factored uniquely into a product of prime numbers (Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic).

steps: To find all factors of 36, test integers starting from 1 up to √36 = 6.
The distinct factors of 36 are {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36}. The greatest proper divisor is 18.
workedExample.result: Factors of 36 are {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36}; its greatest proper divisor is 18.

misconception.mistake: Believing that all odd numbers are prime, or that 2 is not prime because it is even.
misconception.correction: 2 is the only even prime number (its only divisors are 1 and 2). Many odd numbers (like 9, 15, 21, 25, 27) are composite because they have additional factors.

reflection: Prime numbers are the 'atoms' of multiplication: every integer is synthesized from a unique recipe of prime factors.
prerequisiteCheck: Perform whole-number division and verify whether a division leaves a zero remainder.
representation: Take 12 unit squares and build rectangles: 1×12, 2×6, 3×4. Then try with 7 unit squares: only 1×7 is possible, showing that 7 is prime.

faded.prompt: Find the factors of 20: 1 × __ = 20, 2 × __ = 20, 4 × __ = 20. The factors are {1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20}. The greatest proper divisor is __.
faded.solution: 1 × 20 = 20, 2 × 10 = 20, 4 × 5 = 20. The factors are {1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20}. The greatest proper divisor is 10.

independent.prompt: List all factors of 28 and state its greatest proper divisor.
independent.solution: Factors: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. The greatest proper divisor is 14.

independent.prompt: Decompose 60 into its unique prime factorization.

explanation: Explain why if a number n has no prime divisors less than or equal to √n, it is guaranteed to be prime.

transfer.prompt: A baker has 48 muffins and wants to pack them into identical gift boxes with no muffins left over. If each box must contain more than 1 muffin and fewer than 48 muffins, what box sizes are possible?
transfer.solution: Any proper divisor of 48 greater than 1: 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 muffins per box.
